description: The bar chart illustrates the Shapley values for different linguistic features across three multilingual BERT models—mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and a third model represented by light green bars (possibly a baseline or variant, though unlabeled in the legend beyond its color)—as evaluated in the context of morphosyntactic probing. The horizontal axis categorizes linguistic features labeled L₄⁺, L₃, L₂, L₁, T, R₁, R₂, R₃, and R₄⁺, likely representing different layers or types of syntactic or morphological information, possibly ordered by complexity or position in the model. The vertical axis, labeled “Shapley value,” ranges from 0 to 80 with tick marks at intervals of 20, indicating the relative contribution of each feature to model performance as measured by the Shapley value metric. The tallest bar corresponds to the “T” category for the light green model, reaching approximately 80, suggesting it has the highest feature importance in that model. The mBERT and XLM-R models show moderate contributions in “T” (around 60 and 55, respectively) and “L₁” (around 15 each), while most other categories show low values near zero, especially for R₃ and R₄⁺. The bars are grouped by linguistic feature, with each group containing three bars (one per model), allowing for direct comparison of model behavior across features. The chart uses a simple grid and a legend in the upper right to distinguish the models by color, with no additional annotations or error bars.
